title: Ten, Five, Three, Two, Even One
hookLine: your community, or the one you're still looking for
carry: where people gather over torah, the shechinah rests
tomorrow: is "i don't know" allowed in a tradition full of answers?

cards: For two weeks after Owen's grandma died, someone from his church brought dinner every night. Noa noticed it, because when Mr.

Levin died last spring, her synagogue did the same: a sign-up sheet, a casserole, a knock at the door. Two different houses of worship, one very familiar casserole. So what makes a group of people the place you belong?

teach.h: TEN, FIVE, THREE, TWO, EVEN ONE.
teach.b: Pirkei Avot has an answer that counts down. Rabbi Halafta of Kefar Hananiah taught: when ten sit together and busy themselves with Torah, the Shechinah, God's presence, rests among them. Then he goes lower.
Hillel adds the other side in a single line: do not separate yourself from the community. Here's a neighbor saying something close.

teach.h: A NEIGHBOR: TWO OR THREE GATHERED.
teach.b: Christians read in the Gospel of Matthew: "For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them."

What's shared is real: a presence in the gathering, even a very small one, and a reason to show up. The honest difference matters too. In Matthew, Christians hear Jesus himself in the midst of those gathered in his name.
In Avot, the gathering is around words of Torah, and the presence is the Shechinah.
And some Jewish prayers, like Kaddish, wait for ten. Belonging, in both, isn't a crowd that already knows you. It's a table you keep coming back to.
Something to tell a friend tonight: Avot counts all the way down to one.

how: Synagogues, Hillel houses, study partnerships and havurot are common Jewish communities; when someone dies, members often organize meals for the mourners, as churches often do for theirs.

o: the town where you were born and raised
any group that shares all your views
the people you keep coming back to

p: ten, five, three, two, even one
where two or three are gathered

s: in Avot, the presence rests only on a full gathering of ten
Rabbi Halafta counts down to five, three, two, even one.
'where two or three are gathered' is a line from the Talmud
it's from the Gospel of Matthew, read by Christians.
Hillel taught: do not separate yourself from the community

games.q: first friday on campus: a Shabbat dinner, a theater club party, and a game night on your dorm floor. you're new, and nobody knows you yet. what fits Hillel's line?
o: find one table you'll come back to, and keep showing up.
wait until you know some people before joining anything.
drop by all three for ten minutes so nobody feels skipped.
games.why: 'do not separate yourself from the community' asks for a place you return to. Avot says even two sitting together over Torah have a presence among them.

practice: Name your community out loud: the people, the room, the table. If you're still looking, name one place you could try. Then send a short message to one person in it, or one person who might be.

wordCard.voice: Where you belong: the gathering you keep coming back to, where a presence rests, whether ten sit together or two.

carryVoice: Your line: where people gather over Torah, the Shechinah rests. Sometimes a full room, sometimes two people and a book. Shalom for now.

sources.ref: Mishnah Avot 3:6 (Rabbi Halafta of Kefar Hananiah: ten who sit and study, the Shechinah among them; also five, three, two, one)
Mishnah Avot 2:4 (Hillel: do not separate yourself from the community)
